answer_1.quote: For LLMs: Explicit prompts specify the gesture's canonical name, alternate names, and physical description. We evaluate two settings: (1) single-turn prompts, and (2) a two-turn Chain-of-Thought setup getting meaning in first-turn, and then offensiveness classification in the second.

answer_2.quote: For T2I systems, we examine rejection rates -the proportion of generation requests blocked by safety systems. For LLMs and VLMs, models classify gestures into four categories...we measure Recall (true positive rate; TPR) (correct identification of offensive gestures) and Specificity (true negative rate; TNR) (correct identification of non-offensive gestures).

answer_3.quote: We use gpt-4o to classify the presence of such gestures in the outputs. Similarly, for LLMs, gpt-4o is used to detect whether these gestures are suggested.
